name: Marshmallow
grown_as: The wild marsh-mallow, a hardy perennial of damp ground, grown from seed.
habit: An upright perennial 1 to 1.5 m (up to 2 m), several stiff, little-branched stems from the base; the whole plant softly velvety and grey.

leaf.type: Simple, often shallowly three- to five-lobed
leaf.outline: Oval to triangular, 3 to 8 cm long, the lobes shallow
leaf.base: Rounded to broadly wedge-shaped, sometimes slightly heart-shaped
leaf.margin: Irregular, rather blunt teeth all round
leaf.veins: Three to five main veins spreading from the base like a hand, pressed in
leaf.surface: Thick and velvety with soft star-shaped hairs on both sides; often slightly folded

flower.form: A shallow saucer like a small hollyhock
flower.petals: Five, free, broad, slightly notched at the outer edge
flower.centre: A short column of joined stamens with purplish-red anthers
flower.behind: A velvety green calyx of five pointed lobes, with a ring of six to nine narrow pointed extra lobes (the epicalyx) beneath it
flower.carried: In small clusters on short stalks in the upper leaf joints and at the top of the stems, facing up and out

fruit: A flat round ring of segments like a small cheese, sitting in the persistent calyx, green ripening brown. Each segment holds one kidney-shaped brown seed, about 2 mm.
seedling: Two rounded to heart-shaped seed leaves on stalks, then round, toothed, velvety first leaves
winter: Dies down to the ground; the dead stems may stand brown.

leaf: oval to triangular, shallowly lobed leaf with irregular teeth
bloom: five broad pale pink petals in a saucer
a short central column of stamens with purplish anthers
seedling: two rounded to heart-shaped seed leaves
first true leaves round and toothed
young: upright stems of velvety grey-green lobed leaves
flower: pale pink flowers in clusters in the upper leaf joints
seedhead: flat round cheese-like fruits in the dry calyces up the stems
dormant: bare ground or brown dead stems

look_alikes: Common mallow (Malva sylvestris) has larger purple-pink flowers with dark stripes and greener, deeper-lobed leaves. Hollyhock (Alcea rosea) is much taller with big flowers in a spike. Tree-mallow is woody with dark-centred flowers.
